title: Management & Administration
outcomes: Explain registers, beneficial interest and annual return requirements.
Apply the rules for AGMs and EGMs, including requisitions and notices.
Apply quorum, proxy, voting and poll provisions.
Distinguish resolutions and state filing and minute requirements.

meta.exam_tip: Numbers carry marks: 9/6/15 months (AGM), 21/45 days and 3 months (requisition), 21 clear days notice, 5/15/30/2 quorum, 50 members proxy, 14 days special notice, 30 days filing.

concepts.title: Registers, beneficial interest and annual return (ss. 88–95)
body: Section 88: every company keeps registers of members, debenture holders and other security holders, indicating classes of shares; for securities held in demat form, the depository's records serve as the register.

Section 89: a registered holder who does not hold the beneficial interest must declare it to the company (and the beneficial owner must also declare); the company files a return with the Registrar. Section 90: individuals holding significant beneficial ownership (directly or indirectly) must declare it, and the company keeps a register of significant beneficial owners; the Tribunal may restrict rights where information is withheld.

Section 92: every company files an annual return (MGT-7, or MGT-7A for small and one person companies) within 60 days of the AGM, giving registered office, business, holdings, shareholders, directors and KMP, meetings and remuneration. Listed companies and companies above prescribed thresholds have it certified by a practising company secretary.

Section 94: registers and annual returns are kept at the registered office, or at another place in India where more than one-tenth of members reside if a special resolution approves; members may inspect free and take extracts.
concepts.analogy: The registers say who owns the company; the annual return tells the Registrar every year.
concepts.work: A nominee holding shares for a parent must declare the beneficial interest within the prescribed time.

concepts.title: Annual general meeting (ss. 96–97)
body: Section 96: every company other than a one person company holds an annual general meeting each year. The first AGM is held within nine months from the close of the first financial year; later AGMs within six months of the year end, and not more than fifteen months between two AGMs.
The Registrar may, for special reasons, extend the time for any AGM other than the first by up to three months.

An AGM is held during business hours (9 a.m. to 6 p.m.) on a day that is not a national holiday, at the registered office or another place in the city, town or village of the registered office (unlisted companies may hold it anywhere in India with consent of all members).

Section 97: if an AGM is not held, the Tribunal may call or direct it on any member's application. Ordinary business at an AGM is consideration of financial statements and reports, declaration of dividend, appointment of directors in place of those retiring, and appointment and fixing remuneration of auditors; everything else is special business.
concepts.analogy: Once a year, within strict time limits, the members must meet.
concepts.work: A company whose year ends on 31 March must hold its AGM by 30 September.

concepts.title: Extraordinary general meetings, notice and explanatory statement (ss. 98–102)
body: Section 100: the Board may call an extraordinary general meeting whenever it thinks fit. Members holding at least one-tenth of paid-up capital with voting rights (or, for a company without share capital, one-tenth of voting power) may requisition one. If the Board does not, within 21 days, call it for a date within 45 days, the requisitionists may call and hold it within three months, and the company reimburses reasonable expenses.
Section 98: the Tribunal may order a meeting where it is impracticable to call one in the ordinary way.

Section 101: a general meeting needs at least 21 clear days' notice in writing or electronically, stating place, date, day, hour and business, sent to every member, legal representative of deceased members, assignee of an insolvent member, auditors and directors. Shorter notice is allowed with written or electronic consent — for an AGM, of at least 95% of members entitled to vote; for other meetings, of a majority in number of members entitled to vote who hold at least 95% of the paid-up capital carrying voting rights.
Section 102: a statement setting out material facts of special business, including the interest of directors, KMP and their relatives, is annexed to the notice.
concepts.analogy: Members can force a meeting, but only with enough backing and within set time limits.
concepts.work: Notice posted on 1 May allows a meeting on 25 May only if 21 clear days are counted correctly (excluding dispatch and meeting days).

concepts.title: Quorum, chairman, proxies and voting (ss. 103–110)
body: Section 103: unless the articles require more, quorum for a public company is 5 members personally present if members are up to 1,000; 15 if over 1,000 and up to 5,000; and 30 if over 5,000. For a private company it is 2. If no quorum within half an hour, the meeting stands adjourned to the same day next week (or as the Board decides); at the adjourned meeting, those present form the quorum.
Section 104: members elect a chairman by show of hands unless the articles provide otherwise.

Section 105: a member entitled to vote may appoint a proxy, who need not be a member but cannot speak and votes only on a poll. A person may be proxy for not more than 50 members and holding not more than 10% of total voting capital. Proxy forms are deposited at least 48 hours before the meeting.

Sections 107–110: voting is first by show of hands unless e-voting is used; a poll may be ordered by the chairman or demanded by members holding one-tenth of voting power or shares with paid-up value of at least ₹5 lakh. Prescribed companies must offer e-voting. Some items must be passed by postal ballot.
concepts.analogy: Quorum, proxies and polls make sure decisions reflect the members' real voting strength.
concepts.work: A member holding shares worth ₹6 lakh paid-up can demand a poll on his own.

concepts.title: Resolutions, special notice, filing and minutes (ss. 111–122)
body: Section 114: an ordinary resolution needs more votes in favour than against; a special resolution needs votes in favour at least three times votes against, with the intention to propose it as special stated in the notice.

Section 115: where the Act or articles require special notice (such as removal of a director or appointing an auditor other than the retiring one), members holding at least 1% of voting power or shares with paid-up value of ₹5 lakh give notice at least 14 days before the meeting; the company informs members at least 7 days before.

Section 111: members with one-tenth voting power or 100 members holding ₹1 lakh paid-up capital can require circulation of their resolution or statement. Section 116: a resolution passed at an adjourned meeting is treated as passed on that later date.

Section 117: special resolutions and other specified resolutions and agreements are filed with the Registrar within 30 days (MGT-14). Section 118: minutes of every meeting are prepared, signed and kept within 30 days; they are evidence of proceedings. Section 121: listed public companies file a report on each AGM within 30 days. Section 122: a one person company may pass resolutions by entering them in the minute book signed by the sole member.
concepts.analogy: Different decisions need different majorities and must be recorded and filed on time.
concepts.work: A special resolution to change the registered office state must be filed in MGT-14 within 30 days.

illustrations.title: Dates and votes
illustrations.q: (a) Vriksh Ltd. was incorporated on 10 August 2025 and its first financial year ended on 31 March 2026. By when must its first AGM be held? (b) At a general meeting of another company, 130 votes are cast against a resolution and 380 for it; 40 members abstain. Is it a valid special resolution?

head: Point
Rule
Answer
rows: (a) First AGM
Within ₹9 months from close of first financial year
By 31 December 2026 (no extension by the Registrar for the first AGM)
Later AGMs
Within 6 months of year end; gap not over ₹15 months
(b) Special resolution
Votes for must be at least 3 × votes against = ₹390
380 < 390 — not passed as a special resolution (it passes as ordinary)
solution.title: AGM and special resolution

solution.text: Abstentions are ignored in counting votes for a special resolution.

checks.label: First AGM: months from the end of the first financial year
Minimum votes in favour for a special resolution when 130 vote against

illustrations.title: Requisition and quorum
illustrations.q: Members of Aarohan Ltd. (public; 3,000 members; paid-up capital ₹10 crore) holding ₹1.2 crore of paid-up capital requisition an EGM on 1 June. The Board does nothing. (a) Can they call the meeting themselves, and by when? (b) What is the quorum? (c) How many members can one proxy represent?

solution.facts: Requisition by holders of 12% of paid-up capital; Board inactive; 3,000 members.
solution.analysis: Members holding at least one-tenth of paid-up capital carrying voting rights may requisition an EGM. If the Board does not, within 21 days, call a meeting to be held within 45 days of the requisition, the requisitionists may call and hold it within three months of the requisition, recovering expenses from the company. Quorum for a public company with more than 1,000 but up to 5,000 members is 15 personally present. A proxy may act for up to 50 members holding not more than 10% of total share capital with voting rights.
solution.conclusion: (a) Yes — after 22 June and by 1 September. (b) ₹15 members. (c) Up to ₹50 members (and 10% of capital).

checks.label: Maximum members a proxy may act for
Quorum for a public company with 3,000 members

jobs.title: AGM compliance calendar
jobs.situation: You must plan the AGM of an unlisted public company with 2,500 members and a special business item.
steps: Fix the AGM date within six months of year end.
Send 21 clear days' notice with explanatory statement.
Prepare proxy and quorum checks (15 members).
File MGT-14 and the annual return on time.
jobs.takeaway: Every stage of a meeting has its own deadline.

mcqs.q: The first AGM of a company must be held within:
options: Nine months from the close of its first financial year
mcqs.explain: Section 96 requires the first AGM within nine months from the close of the first financial year; later AGMs within six months of year end. The Registrar cannot extend the time for the first AGM. In practice: diarise from incorporation.

mcqs.q: The gap between two AGMs must not exceed:
mcqs.explain: Section 96 provides that not more than fifteen months shall elapse between the dates of two consecutive AGMs, apart from the six-month rule. In practice: check both limits.

mcqs.q: Members can requisition an EGM if they hold at least:
options: One-tenth of paid-up capital with voting rights
mcqs.explain: Section 100 lets members holding at least one-tenth of the paid-up share capital carrying voting rights requisition an EGM. In practice: deposit a signed requisition at the registered office.
mcqs.topic: Extraordinary general meetings, notice and explanatory statement (ss. 98–102)

mcqs.q: Notice of a general meeting must normally be given at least:
mcqs.explain: Section 101 requires at least 21 clear days' notice in writing or electronic mode; shorter notice is possible with the required consent of members. In practice: exclude the day of service and the meeting day.
mcqs.topic: Extraordinary general meetings, notice and explanatory statement (ss. 98–102)

mcqs.q: Quorum for a public company with 7,000 members (articles silent):
mcqs.explain: Section 103 sets 30 members personally present where members exceed 5,000, 15 for 1,001–5,000, and 5 for up to 1,000. Private companies need 2. In practice: count only those present in person.

mcqs.q: A proxy can act for at most:
options: 50 members holding not more than 10% of voting capital
mcqs.explain: Section 105 and the rules limit a proxy to acting for 50 members, together holding not more than 10% of total share capital carrying voting rights. In practice: check proxy forms 48 hours before.

mcqs.q: A special resolution requires votes in favour to be at least:
options: Seventy-five per cent of all members
mcqs.explain: Under section 114, a special resolution needs votes cast in favour of at least three times the votes cast against, with the intention stated in the notice. Abstentions are ignored. In practice: count valid votes only.
mcqs.topic: Resolutions, special notice, filing and minutes (ss. 111–122)

mcqs.q: Special notice of a resolution must be given to the company at least:
mcqs.explain: Section 115 requires the notice of intention to move such a resolution at least 14 days before the meeting; the company then informs members at least 7 days before. In practice: used to remove directors.
mcqs.topic: Resolutions, special notice, filing and minutes (ss. 111–122)

mcqs.q: Special resolutions must be filed with the Registrar within:
mcqs.explain: Section 117 requires a copy of every special resolution and other specified resolutions or agreements to be filed with the Registrar within 30 days in Form MGT-14. In practice: attach the explanatory statement.
mcqs.topic: Resolutions, special notice, filing and minutes (ss. 111–122)

mcqs.q: The annual return under section 92 is filed within:
options: 60 days from the date of the AGM
mcqs.explain: Every company files its annual return within sixty days of the AGM (or the last date it should have been held), in MGT-7 or MGT-7A. In practice: certification is required for larger companies.
mcqs.topic: Registers, beneficial interest and annual return (ss. 88–95)

questions.q: Distinguish ordinary business and special business at an AGM.

head: Ordinary business
Special business
rows: Consideration of financial statements and reports of the Board and auditors
Any business other than the four ordinary items
Declaration of dividend
Needs an explanatory statement under section 102
Appointment of directors retiring by rotation
Examples: alteration of articles, issue of shares, related party approvals
Appointment of auditors and fixing their remuneration
Business at any EGM is always special
model.title: AGM business

mistakes: Treating alteration of articles as ordinary.

summary: Registers of members; beneficial interest and SBO declarations; annual return within 60 days of AGM.
First AGM within 9 months of first year end; then 6 months / 15 months; ROC extension up to 3 months (not first).
EGM requisition by 1/10 of paid-up capital; Board 21 days / 45 days; requisitionists within 3 months.
Notice 21 clear days; shorter with 95% consent; explanatory statement for special business.
Quorum 5/15/30 (public), 2 (private); proxy ≤ 50 members, 10%; poll on 1/10 or ₹5 lakh.
Special resolution ≥ 3× against; special notice 14 days; MGT-14 in 30 days; minutes in 30 days.
remember: A proxy cannot speak and votes only on a poll.
traps: The Registrar cannot extend the first AGM.

viva.q: Within what time are AGMs held after the first?
viva.model: Within six months after the financial year ends, with no more than fifteen months between two AGMs.

viva.q: What can requisitionists do if the Board ignores their requisition?
viva.model: If the Board does not within 21 days call a meeting for a date within 45 days, they may themselves call and hold it within three months, recovering expenses.

viva.q: What is the quorum for a private company?
viva.model: Two members personally present, unless the articles require more.
Members present in person or by proxy holding at least one-tenth of the total voting power, or shares with paid-up value of at least ₹5 lakh.
Those requiring it under the Act or articles, such as removal of a director or appointment of an auditor other than the retiring auditor; notice is given at least 14 days before the meeting.

points.pt: Removal of director or auditor change

cases.title: Sumeru Ltd.
cases.case: Sumeru Ltd. (public, 900 members) held its last AGM on 20 August 2025. Its year ends on 31 March 2026. At its 2026 AGM, 4 members are present in person and 20 by proxy; a proxy holder wants to speak against a resolution.

mcqs.q: The 2026 AGM must be held by:
mcqs.explain: Within six months of year end gives 30 September 2026; fifteen months from the last AGM gives 20 November 2026; the earlier date applies. In practice: check both limits.

options: No, 5 members must be personally present
Quorum is not needed for an AGM
mcqs.explain: For a public company with up to 1,000 members, quorum is 5 members personally present; proxies do not count. In practice: wait half an hour, then adjourn.

mcqs.q: May the proxy speak at the meeting?
mcqs.explain: Section 105 states that a proxy shall not have a right to speak at the meeting and may vote only on a poll. In practice: the member must attend to speak.
